canonical_facts: Bundle Active does not guarantee DS component Active.
Delayed DS Satisfied can be normal before first consumer.
A workflow launcher starts a workflow when configured repository-event conditions match.
Sync updates runtime model used by new workflow instances.
Sling Job processing is at least once; retries depend on queue policy.
No custom Cloud log file: send custom Java logs to error.log.

slides.title: An active bundle does not prove an active service
key_points: Bundle Installed: inspect unresolved package imports.
Bundle Resolved: imports are resolved; the bundle is not active.
DS Unsatisfied: inspect required references and configuration.
A delayed DS component can be Satisfied until a consumer requests it.

slides.title: A workflow has a model, a payload and an instance
key_points: Model: the process definition. Payload: the object being processed.
Instance: one execution with its own history and current step.
Sync prepares the runtime model; start a new instance after model changes.
Inspect Instances, Archive or Failures according to the observed state.

slides.title: A process step runs code; a participant step waits
key_points: Process Step: executes a registered WorkflowProcess service.
Participant Step: assigns work to a user or group.
Example: Start → Log payload → End, with Handler Advance enabled.
A log entry proves the step executed; check history to prove completion.

Keep the path narrow and prevent self-triggering changes.

slides.title: Sling Jobs decouple submission from processing
key_points: A producer submits a topic and serializable properties.
A consumer handles that topic and returns a processing result.
OK: success. FAILED: eligible for configured retry. CANCEL: permanent failure.
The processing guarantee is at least once; repeated execution is possible.

slides.title: Retry only after understanding the side effect
key_points: Identify payload, current state, attempt and failure cause.
Fix the cause before retrying a workflow step or job.
Repeating the same operation must not duplicate its business effect.
A timeout does not prove the remote operation never happened.
